name: Kulaale
confidence_why: One first-hand description, checked against the source; 3 other works consulted do not discuss stress.
catalog_citation: Lionnet, Florian. 2020. Kulaale (Chad) – Language Snapshot. In Peter K. Austin (ed.), Language Documentation and Description 17, 126-133. London: EL Publishing. DOI 10.25894/LDD103; open-access copy HAL halshs-04370663 (CC BY-NC 4.0).
catalog_locator: §2 'Current research', p. 131 (bulleted list of preliminary findings); §1 'Overview', p. 130 (prior documentation: four wordlists, tone not transcribed)
catalog_quote: I carried out preliminary fieldwork in Tilé Nougar in 2014 (one day), 2017 (one week), and 2020 (one week). The preliminary data shows that: Kulaale vowels have an advanced tongue root (ATR) contrast and harmony; the tone system is characterized by two contrastive heights, with frequent use of polar tone and complex non-concatenative tonal morphology; verbs have complex morphology with three moods (indicative, subjunctive, infinitive), and a derived instrumental form (‘do X with’), in all three moods; a focus suffix is used on all verbal forms (simple and associative forms, all moods) when an element in the utterance is focused. [p. 130] Kulaale is virtually undocumented. Before my visits to Tilé Nougar in 2014 (24 hours), 2017 (one week) and 2020 (one week), only four wordlists had been collected: Gaudefroy-Demombynes (1906:107) of 200 words, Joly (1935) of 200 words, Faris & Meundeung (1993) of 160 words, and 50 words collected by Chadian linguist Khalil Alio in 2005. All except the last use unreliable transcriptions (e.g. advanced tongue root (ATR) contrasts for vowels are not identified, tone is not transcribed).
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

[bullet] a focus suffix..' (the compiler quote only flattens the four bullets into one sentence and marks the omitted…
new_statements.rule_in_words: Fania/Kulaale is a tone language with two contrastive pitch heights (H/L), polar tone and grammatical (non-concatenative) tonal morphology. No source examined says anything about word stress or accent placement — neither a rule, nor that stress is non-contrastive, nor that it is absent. The only modern first-hand description is a 2020 language snapshot based on about two weeks of fieldwork; the reference grammar from the 2020-2025 NSF project has not appeared.
new_statements.exceptions: None; no stress rule is given.
new_statements.domain_note: Tone statement is about the lexical/grammatical tone system (word level); Boyeldieu et al. 2018 (Table 3, p.5-6) add second-hand that Kulaale/Fanya contrasts mood/aspect on the verb by tone change. Nothing about phrase-level prominence.
new_statements.identity_note: Lionnet's 'Kulaale' [kʊ̀láálɛ́] (speakers Kulaawe/Eywe) is the same language as Glottolog fani1244 'Fania' [fni]; his data come from the single village of Tilé Nougar (blacksmith community). Boyeldieu et al. 2018 reserve 'Kulaale' for Lionnet's data and 'Fanya' for older sources (Joly 1935; Faris & Meundeung 1993c from Rim and Sissi; Khalil Alio's list) and note variation among Fanya varieties (h- ~ f-). Do not confuse with Kulaal = Gula Iro (gula1265 [glj]), a different Bua language whose stress/tone statement (Pairault 1969) is already recorded under gula1265.

tone_statements.citation: Lionnet, Florian. 2023. L'inventaire phonologique du fanya (boua, Tchad): description et données comparatives préliminaires. Paper presented at the Séminaire du LLACAN (CNRS - INALCO - EPHE), Villejuif/Paris, 18 January 2023. Abstract published on the LLACAN blog (llacan.cnrs.fr/blog/?p=1893, posted 10 January 2023).
tone_statements.quote: Les caractéristiques phonologiques les plus importantes du kulaale sont décrites, à savoir : ... (iv) un système tonal opposant deux registres, ainsi qu’une morphologie tonale complexe, en particulier dans le système verbal. ... Le système vocalique semble directement hérité du proto-boua, sans grand changement (c’est peut-être également le cas du système tonal, bien que les données soient moins claires à ce sujet).
tone_statements.translation: The most important phonological characteristics of Kulaale are described, namely: ... (iv) a tone system opposing two registers, as well as a complex tonal morphology, in particular in the verbal system. ... The vowel system seems to be directly inherited from Proto-Bua without much change (this may also be the case for the tone system, although the data are less clear on this point).
tone_statements.summary: 2 level tones (two registers) + complex tonal (verbal) morphology.

tone_statements.citation: Boyeldieu, Pascal. 2020. Personal pronouns in Bua languages. Language in Africa 1(3) (Special issue on the Adamawa languages): 292-335. Moscow: Institute of Linguistics RAS. DOI 10.37892/2686-8946-2020-1-3-292-335. Open-access copy: HAL halshs-03097103.
tone_statements.quote: — Tonally, all independent pronouns are LH; indicative subject pronouns are all H except 1p ɔ̀; subjunctive subject pronouns are all L; Object/possessive pronouns are all L, except 3s ɛ́; Emphatic possessive pronouns are all HLH. ... In Lua, Tun, Ɓa, Kulaal, and Kulaalɛ, the major division Subject/ Object is chiefly marked by tone contrasts. ... — Subject = High (Tun Mid) vs. Object = Low ... ‣ Kulaalɛ (indicative subject only): 1s, 2s, 2p, and 3p (1p is always L-toned, and 3s Subject/Object have different forms and same tone)
tone_statements.locator: p. 309, section 6 'Kulaalɛ' (bullet list completing Table 7); pp. 327-328, section 13.2.1
tone_statements.summary: Pronoun paradigms distinguished by tone: subject H vs object/possessive L (indicative), subjunctive subject L, independent LH, emphatic possessive HLH; data show H/L only.

sources.note: Nothing on stress or accent. §2 'Current research' (p.131) reports from 2014/2017/2020 fieldwork in Tilé Nougar that vowels have ATR harmony and 'the tone system is characterized by two contrastive heights, with frequent use of polar tone and complex non-concatenative tonal morphology'. p.130: the language is 'virtually undocumented'; the only prior data are four short wordlists (Gaudefroy-Demombynes 1906, Joly 1935, Faris & Meundeung 1993, Khalil Alio 2005), 'tone is not transcribed' in all but the last.
No descriptive references at all (only classification/overview works); AES status 'shifting' citing Lionnet 2020; alternative names include Kulaale, Eywe, Fanya, Mana, Kobe.

sources.note: First descriptive sketch of Fanya (Kulaale dialect) phonology from 2014-2022 fieldwork; item (iv) states a tone system opposing two registers (two level tones) plus complex tonal morphology especially in the verb system; adds that the tone system may, like the vowel system, be inherited from Proto-Bua with little change, though the data are less clear. Also: plosive-poor consonant system with heavy allophony; 9 vowels with ATR contrast (5 [-ATR] /ɪ ɛ a ɔ ʊ/, 4 [+ATR] /i e o u/); dominant [+ATR] harmony. Nothing on stress/accent in the abstract.
